notes: The italicized second 'thy' is no longer 'added': ἐξ ἀριστερῶν is anarthrous, so rule 51's anarthrous clause makes the supplied possessive a rule 7 helper on the substantival adjective it determines, matching this chapter's own treatment of γυναῖκα → 'his wife' at 10:2 under rule 24's habit. Rule 103 is scoped to supplied lexical content and names a pronoun as the contrast that folds.

Reading the second 'thy' as a discontinuous second realization of σου under rules 15 and 76 stays defensible; what is not defensible is 'added', which rules 11 and 20 warn against for a supplied possessive.
